items.stem: What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
items.answer: Al₂O₃

items.stem: Explain why brackets are needed in the formula Ca(OH)₂ but not in NaOH.
items.answer: Two hydroxide ions are needed to balance Ca²⁺; the bracket shows that the subscript 2 applies to the whole OH group. NaOH contains only one OH⁻, so no bracket is needed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: two OH⁻ to balance 2+; 1 mark: bracket applies subscript to whole group [2]

items.stem: A student writes the formula of magnesium chloride as MgCl. Explain the error and give the correct formula.
items.answer: Mg forms Mg²⁺ and chloride is Cl⁻, so two chloride ions are needed: MgCl₂.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: charges; 1 mark: MgCl₂ [2]

items.stem: Use the charges on the ions to write the formula of each compound: silver phosphate, lead(II) phosphate.
items.answer: silver phosphate: Ag₃PO₄; lead(II) phosphate: Pb₃(PO₄)₂
items.markingKey: silver phosphate: Ag₃PO₄; lead(II) phosphate: Pb₃(PO₄)₂. 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Use the ion charges given to write the formula of each compound: iron(II) iodide (Fe²⁺, I⁻), calcium hydroxide (Ca²⁺, OH⁻), calcium bromide (Ca²⁺, Br⁻).
items.answer: iron(II) iodide: FeI₂; calcium hydroxide: Ca(OH)₂; calcium bromide: CaBr₂
items.markingKey: iron(II) iodide: FeI₂; calcium hydroxide: Ca(OH)₂; calcium bromide: CaBr₂. 1 mark each [3]

items.stem: Using the ion charges shown in brackets, to write the formula of each compound: calcium sulfide (Ca²⁺, S²⁻), copper(II) sulfate (Cu²⁺, SO₄²⁻), copper(II) chloride (Cu²⁺, Cl⁻), lead(II) sulfide (Pb²⁺, S²⁻).
items.answer: calcium sulfide: CaS; copper(II) sulfate: CuSO₄; copper(II) chloride: CuCl₂; lead(II) sulfide: PbS
items.markingKey: calcium sulfide: CaS; copper(II) sulfate: CuSO₄; copper(II) chloride: CuCl₂; lead(II) sulfide: PbS. 1 mark each [4]

items.stem: A technician in Kathmandu needs formulae for three compounds: lithium nitrate, iron(III) chloride and aluminium bromide. (a) Calculate the relative formula mass of iron(III) chloride. (b) Explain why the formula of aluminium bromide contains the ions in that ratio.
items.answer: (a) 162.5 (b) the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge (compound is neutral)

items.stem: Ravi is labelling bottles of chemicals in a college laboratory. The bottles contain silver bromide, iron(III) oxide and magnesium oxide. (a) Give the formula and charge of each ion present in the three compounds. (b) Explain why the formula of magnesium oxide contains the ions in that ratio.
items.answer: (a) Ag⁺, Br⁻; Fe³⁺, O²⁻; Mg²⁺, O²⁻ (b) the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge (compound is neutral)
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per compound [3] (b) [2]

items.stem: What is the formula of the sulfate ion?
items.answer: SO₄²⁻
items.markingKey: Sulfate: SO₄²⁻.

items.stem: What is the formula of ammonium sulfate?
items.answer: (NH₄)₂SO₄
items.markingKey: NH₄⁺ and SO₄²⁻: two ammonium ions per sulfate.

items.stem: Explain how the formula of a compound of iron(III) can be deduced from its name, using iron(III) sulfate as an example.
items.answer: The Roman numeral shows the ion is Fe³⁺; sulfate is SO₄²⁻; the lowest ratio giving zero charge is 2 Fe³⁺ : 3 SO₄²⁻, so Fe₂(SO₄)₃.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Fe³⁺ from numeral; 1 mark: charge balance → Fe₂(SO₄)₃ [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between the formulae 2H₂O and H₂O₂.
items.answer: 2H₂O means two molecules of water (4 H and 2 O atoms in total); H₂O₂ is one molecule of hydrogen peroxide containing 2 H and 2 O atoms.

items.stem: Explain how the valency of carbon and oxygen can be used to deduce the formula of carbon dioxide.
items.answer: Carbon has valency 4 and oxygen valency 2, so one carbon combines with two oxygens (each forming a double bond): CO₂.

items.stem: Daniel, a student in Singapore, is told that nitrogen has a valency of 3 and hydrogen has a valency of 1. Deduce the formula of the covalent compound formed and explain how many bonds each atom makes.
items.answer: NH₃ (ammonia): each nitrogen atom forms 3 bond(s) and each hydrogen atom forms 1; the numbers of bonds must match.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: formula NH₃; 1 mark: bonds per atom = valency; 1 mark: ratio so total bonds match [3]

items.stem: State the number of atoms of each element in the formula Mg(NO₃)₂, and the total number of atoms.
items.answer: Mg 1, N 2, O 6; total 9
items.markingKey: Mg 1, N 2, O 6 [1]; total 9 [1]

items.stem: Use the charges on the ions to write the formula of each compound: calcium nitride, iron(II) oxide.
items.answer: calcium nitride: Ca₃N₂; iron(II) oxide: FeO
items.markingKey: calcium nitride: Ca₃N₂; iron(II) oxide: FeO. 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: State the number of atoms of each element in the formula Ca(OH)₂, and the total number of atoms.
items.answer: Ca 1, O 2, H 2; total 5
items.markingKey: Ca 1, O 2, H 2 [1]; total 5 [1]

items.stem: Using the ion charges shown in brackets, to write the formula of each compound: aluminium iodide (Al³⁺, I⁻), potassium bromide (K⁺, Br⁻), iron(II) phosphate (Fe²⁺, PO₄³⁻).
items.answer: aluminium iodide: AlI₃; potassium bromide: KBr; iron(II) phosphate: Fe₃(PO₄)₂
items.markingKey: aluminium iodide: AlI₃; potassium bromide: KBr; iron(II) phosphate: Fe₃(PO₄)₂. 1 mark each [3]

items.stem: Priya is labelling bottles of chemicals in an IGCSE practical lesson. The bottles contain copper(II) phosphate, potassium bromide and zinc phosphate. (a) State the total number of atoms in the formula of copper(II) phosphate. (b) Explain why the formula of a compound containing a polyatomic ion sometimes needs brackets. (c) Explain why the formula of zinc phosphate contains the ions in that ratio.
items.answer: (a) 13 (b) to show that the subscript multiplies the whole group of atoms in the ion (c) the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge (compound is neutral)

items.stem: A technician in Lisbon needs formulae for three compounds: barium fluoride, aluminium oxide and calcium carbonate. (a) Give the formula and charge of each ion present in the three compounds. (b) Explain why the formula of calcium carbonate contains the ions in that ratio.
items.answer: (a) Ba²⁺, F⁻; Al³⁺, O²⁻; Ca²⁺, CO₃²⁻ (b) the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge (compound is neutral)
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per compound [3] (b) [2]

items.stem: What does the state symbol (aq) mean?
items.answer: dissolved in water
items.markingKey: (aq) = aqueous solution.

items.stem: A student balances H₂ + O₂ → H₂O by writing H₂ + O₂ → H₂O₂. Explain why this is wrong and give the correct equation.
items.answer: Changing H₂O to H₂O₂ changes the substance (hydrogen peroxide). Only coefficients may be changed: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: cannot change formula; 1 mark: correct equation [2]

items.stem: Explain why the total mass seems to decrease when calcium carbonate is heated in an open crucible.
items.answer: Carbon dioxide gas is produced and escapes into the air; mass is conserved but the gas is not weighed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: CO₂ gas escapes; 1 mark: mass conserved overall [2]

items.stem: Balance the equation: Cl₂ + KBr → KCl + Br₂
items.answer: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂
items.markingKey: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂ [1]

items.stem: Write the balanced symbol equation, with state symbols, for the reaction: copper(II) oxide + sulfuric acid → copper(II) sulfate + water.
items.answer: CuO(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → CuSO₄(aq) + H₂O(l)
items.markingKey: CuO(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → CuSO₄(aq) + H₂O(l): 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balancing; 1 mark state symbols [3]

items.stem: Write the balanced symbol equation, with state symbols, for the reaction: copper(II) carbonate → copper(II) oxide + carbon dioxide. State the total number of atoms on each side of your equation.
items.answer: CuCO₃(s) → CuO(s) + CO₂(g); 5 atoms on each side
items.markingKey: CuCO₃(s) → CuO(s) + CO₂(g): 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balancing; 1 mark state symbols; 1 mark: 5 atoms each side [4]

items.stem: In a school laboratory in Hanoi, students study the reaction magnesium + steam → magnesium oxide + hydrogen. (a) State the number of atoms of each element on the left-hand side. (b) Calculate the relative formula mass of H₂O. (Ar: H = 1, O = 16) (c) Explain why the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products. (d) Suggest why the mass of the reaction container may change if the reaction is done in an open beaker.
items.answer: (a) H 2, Mg 1, O 1 (b) 18 (c) atoms are rearranged; none are created or destroyed (d) a gas is given off / taken in from the air

items.stem: In a college laboratory in Nairobi, students study the reaction magnesium + steam → magnesium oxide + hydrogen. (a) Write the balanced symbol equation, including state symbols. (b) State the number of atoms of each element on the left-hand side. (c) Explain why the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
items.answer: (a) Mg(s) + H₂O(g) → MgO(s) + H₂(g) (b) H 2, Mg 1, O 1 (c) atoms are rearranged; none are created or destroyed
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balanced; 1 mark state symbols [3] (b) [1] (c) [1]

items.stem: Why must a chemical equation be balanced?
options: The number of substances must be equal.
Atoms are not created or destroyed in a reaction.
The volumes of gases must be equal.
Molecules are not created or destroyed.
items.answer: Atoms are not created or destroyed in a reaction.
items.markingKey: Conservation of mass: same numbers of each atom on each side.

items.stem: Explain why the total mass stays the same when silver nitrate solution is added to sodium chloride solution in a closed flask.
items.answer: No atoms are gained or lost; all products, including the precipitate, stay in the flask.

items.stem: Explain what the coefficient 2 in 2NaOH tells you.
items.answer: There are two formula units of sodium hydroxide, i.e. 2 Na, 2 O and 2 H atoms (2 mol in mole terms).

items.stem: Explain why magnesium increases in mass when it is burned in air.
items.answer: Magnesium combines with oxygen from the air to form magnesium oxide; the oxygen atoms add to the mass.

items.stem: Samuel writes the equation for "hydrogen peroxide → water + oxygen" as H₂O₂ → H₂O + O₂. Explain why the equation is not acceptable and write it correctly with state symbols.
items.answer: It is not balanced: the numbers of atoms of each element are not equal on both sides. Correct: 2H₂O₂(aq) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: not balanced / atoms not conserved; 1 mark: correct coefficients; 1 mark: state symbols [3]

items.stem: Amara carries out the reaction C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O in a closed container. The masses of the substances that react and are formed are: C₂H₅OH: 92 g; O₂: ?; CO₂: 176 g; H₂O: 108 g. Calculate the missing mass and state the law you used.
items.answer: 192 g; conservation of mass (total mass of reactants 284 g = total mass of products).
items.markingKey: mass of reactants = mass of products (conservation of mass) [1]; missing mass = 192 g [1]

items.stem: Balance the equation: Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃
items.answer: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃
items.markingKey: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃ [2]

items.stem: Write the balanced symbol equation, with state symbols, for the reaction: calcium carbonate + hydrochloric acid → calcium chloride + water + carbon dioxide.
items.answer: CaCO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g)
items.markingKey: CaCO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g): 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balancing; 1 mark state symbols [3]

items.stem: Kwame carries out the reaction C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O in a closed container. The masses of the substances that react and are formed are: C₂H₅OH: 23 g; O₂: ?; CO₂: 44 g; H₂O: 27 g. Calculate the missing mass and state the law you used.
items.answer: 48 g; conservation of mass (total mass of reactants 71 g = total mass of products).
items.markingKey: mass of reactants = mass of products (conservation of mass) [1]; missing mass = 48 g [1]

items.stem: Omar carries out the reaction 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ in a closed container. The masses of the substances that react and are formed are: Al: 21.6 g; O₂: ?; Al₂O₃: 40.8 g. Calculate the missing mass and state the law you used. Explain, in terms of atoms, why this law applies.
items.answer: 19.2 g; conservation of mass (total mass of reactants 40.8 g = total mass of products).
items.markingKey: mass of reactants = mass of products (conservation of mass) [1]; missing mass = 19.2 g [1]; atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed [1]

items.stem: Isla investigates the reaction: calcium + water → calcium hydroxide + hydrogen. (a) State the number of atoms of each element on the left-hand side. (b) Calculate the relative formula mass of H₂O. (Ar: H = 1, O = 16) (c) Explain why the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products. (d) Suggest why the mass of the reaction container may change if the reaction is done in an open beaker.
items.answer: (a) Ca 1, H 4, O 2 (b) 18 (c) atoms are rearranged; none are created or destroyed (d) a gas is given off / taken in from the air

items.stem: Ana investigates the reaction: aluminium + hydrochloric acid → aluminium chloride + hydrogen. (a) Write the balanced symbol equation, including state symbols. (b) State the number of atoms of each element on the left-hand side. (c) Explain why the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products. (d) Suggest why the mass of the reaction container may change if the reaction is done in an open beaker.
items.answer: (a) 2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2AlCl₃(aq) + 3H₂(g) (b) Al 2, Cl 6, H 6 (c) atoms are rearranged; none are created or destroyed (d) a gas is given off / taken in from the air
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balanced; 1 mark state symbols [3] (b) [1] (c) [1] (d) [1]

items.stem: What is a spectator ion?
options: an ion that is formed from water
an ion present in the reaction mixture that does not take part in the reaction
an ion that forms a precipitate
items.answer: an ion present in the reaction mixture that does not take part in the reaction
items.markingKey: Spectator ions are unchanged; they are left out of the ionic equation.

items.stem: Explain why the ionic equation for the reaction of nitric acid with sodium hydroxide is the same as that for hydrochloric acid with potassium hydroxide.
items.answer: In both, the only change is H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O; the metal ions and the acid anions are spectator ions that remain in solution unchanged.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O; 1 mark: other ions are spectators [2]

items.stem: Explain why silver chloride is written as AgCl(s), not as separate ions, in an ionic equation.
items.answer: It is an insoluble solid (precipitate); its ions are held in a lattice and are not free in solution.

items.stem: The full equation for the neutralisation of sulfuric acid by sodium hydroxide is H₂SO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l). Write the ionic equation for this reaction, including state symbols, and identify the spectator ions.
items.answer: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l); spectator ions: Na⁺ and SO₄²⁻
items.markingKey: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l): 1 mark species; 1 mark balanced with states; 1 mark spectators Na⁺ and SO₄²⁻ [3]

items.stem: The full equation for the reaction of magnesium with copper(II) sulfate solution is Mg(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → MgSO₄(aq) + Cu(s). Write the ionic equation for this reaction, including state symbols, and identify the spectator ions.
items.answer: Mg(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + Cu(s); spectator ions: SO₄²⁻
items.markingKey: Mg(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Mg²⁺(aq) + Cu(s): 1 mark species; 1 mark balanced with states; 1 mark spectators SO₄²⁻ [3]

items.stem: In an IGCSE practical lesson, a student carries out the precipitation of silver chloride from silver nitrate and sodium chloride: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃. (a) List all the ions present in the reactant solutions. (b) Identify the spectator ions. (c) Show that the ionic equation is balanced for charge. (d) Describe what would be observed during the reaction.
items.answer: (a) all ions from the aqueous reactants, e.g. Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ and the reacting ions (b) Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ (c) total charge on the left equals total charge on the right (d) a precipitate forms

items.stem: Which ionic equation represents the neutralisation of any acid by any alkali?
items.answer: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l)
items.markingKey: The H⁺ from the acid reacts with OH⁻ from the alkali.

items.stem: Which substances are shown as separate ions in an ionic equation?
options: ionic compounds that are dissolved in water (aqueous)
items.answer: ionic compounds that are dissolved in water (aqueous)
items.markingKey: Solids, liquids, gases and molecular substances are written as formulae.

items.stem: Explain how an ionic equation can be checked to make sure it is balanced.
items.answer: The numbers of each type of atom and the total charge must both be the same on each side.

items.stem: A student writes the ionic equation for zinc reacting with copper(II) sulfate as Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Explain why this is not an ionic equation and give the correct one.
items.answer: It includes the sulfate spectator ion within formulae; the ionic equation is Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: spectator not removed; 1 mark: correct ionic equation [2]

items.stem: For the reaction of sodium carbonate solution with hydrochloric acid, Na₂CO₃(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g), explain why Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are not included in the ionic equation, and write the ionic equation.
items.answer: Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are present in the same form, dissolved in solution, before and after the reaction (spectator ions). Ionic equation: 2H⁺(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq) → H₂O(l) + CO₂(g).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: spectator meaning; 1 mark: ions that react identified; 1 mark: ionic equation with states [3]

items.stem: Arjun mixes aqueous silver nitrate with aqueous sodium bromide. A precipitate of silver bromide forms. Write the full balanced equation and the ionic equation, each with state symbols.
items.answer: AgNO₃ + NaBr → AgBr + NaNO₃; Ag⁺(aq) + Br⁻(aq) → AgBr(s)
items.markingKey: full: AgNO₃ + NaBr → AgBr + NaNO₃ [1]; state symbols [1]; ionic: Ag⁺(aq) + Br⁻(aq) → AgBr(s) [1]

items.stem: The full equation for the reaction of iron with copper(II) sulfate solution is Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s). Write the ionic equation for this reaction, including state symbols, and identify the spectator ions.
items.answer: Fe(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Fe²⁺(aq) + Cu(s); spectator ions: SO₄²⁻
items.markingKey: Fe(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Fe²⁺(aq) + Cu(s): 1 mark species; 1 mark balanced with states; 1 mark spectators SO₄²⁻ [3]

items.stem: Isla investigates the reaction of zinc with sulfuric acid. The full equation is Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. (a) Add state symbols to the full equation. (b) Identify the spectator ions. (c) Describe what would be observed during the reaction.
items.answer: (a) Zn(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + H₂(g) (b) SO₄²⁻ (c) see observations: e.g. fizzing / colour change / temperature rise

items.stem: In a college laboratory, a student carries out the reaction of magnesium with hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. (a) List all the ions present in the reactant solutions. (b) Identify the spectator ions. (c) Show that the ionic equation is balanced for charge. (d) Describe what would be observed during the reaction.
items.answer: (a) all ions from the aqueous reactants, e.g. Cl⁻ and the reacting ions (b) Cl⁻ (c) total charge on the left equals total charge on the right (d) see observations: e.g. fizzing / colour change / temperature rise

items.stem: Which ion has a charge of 3−?
items.answer: phosphate
items.markingKey: PO₄³⁻ (also nitride N³⁻).

items.stem: Hydrogen has a valency of 1 and sulfur a valency of 2. Deduce the formula of the compound they form and explain your reasoning.
items.answer: H₂S
items.markingKey: Combining powers must match: H₂S (hydrogen sulfide) [2]

items.stem: Kwame, a student in Karachi, is told that carbon has a valency of 4 and sulfur has a valency of 2. Deduce the formula of the covalent compound formed and explain how many bonds each atom makes.
items.answer: CS₂ (carbon disulfide): each carbon atom forms 4 bond(s) and each sulfur atom forms 2; the numbers of bonds must match.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: formula CS₂; 1 mark: bonds per atom = valency; 1 mark: ratio so total bonds match [3]

items.stem: State the number of atoms of each element in the formula C₂H₅OH, and the total number of atoms.
items.answer: C 2, H 6, O 1; total 9

items.stem: Use the charges on the ions to write the formula of each compound: zinc sulfate, iron(III) oxide.
items.answer: zinc sulfate: ZnSO₄; iron(III) oxide: Fe₂O₃
items.markingKey: zinc sulfate: ZnSO₄; iron(III) oxide: Fe₂O₃. 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: State the number of atoms of each element in the formula Na₃PO₄, and the total number of atoms.
items.answer: Na 3, P 1, O 4; total 8
items.markingKey: Na 3, P 1, O 4 [1]; total 8 [1]

items.stem: Tomás is labelling bottles of chemicals in an IGCSE practical lesson. The bottles contain sodium iodide, sodium carbonate and barium chloride. (a) State the total number of atoms in the formula of sodium iodide. (b) Explain why the formula of a compound containing a polyatomic ion sometimes needs brackets. (c) Explain why the formula of barium chloride contains the ions in that ratio.
items.answer: (a) 2 (b) to show that the subscript multiplies the whole group of atoms in the ion (c) the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge (compound is neutral)

items.stem: Sipho is labelling bottles of chemicals in a teaching laboratory. The bottles contain copper(II) chloride, lead(II) fluoride and sodium hydroxide. (a) Give the formula and charge of each ion present in the three compounds. (b) State the total number of atoms in the formula of copper(II) chloride. (c) Explain why the formula of sodium hydroxide contains the ions in that ratio.
items.answer: (a) Cu²⁺, Cl⁻; Pb²⁺, F⁻; Na⁺, OH⁻ (b) 3 (c) the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge (compound is neutral)
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per compound [3] (b) [1] (c) [2]

items.stem: Which state symbol should be used for water at room temperature?
items.markingKey: Water is a liquid at room temperature.

items.stem: Priya writes the equation for "magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide" as Mg + O₂ → MgO. Explain why the equation is not acceptable and write it correctly with state symbols.
items.answer: It is not balanced: the numbers of atoms of each element are not equal on both sides. Correct: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: not balanced; 1 mark: correct balanced equation [2]

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain what the coefficient 2 in 2NaOH tells you. (b) Explain why the total mass stays the same when silver nitrate solution is added to sodium chloride solution in a closed flask.
items.answer: (a) There are two formula units of sodium hydroxide, i.e. 2 Na, 2 O and 2 H atoms (2 mol in mole terms). (b) No atoms are gained or lost; all products, including the precipitate, stay in the flask.

items.stem: Tariq carries out the reaction CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂ in a closed container. The masses of the substances that react and are formed are: CaCO₃: ?; HCl: 14.6 g; CaCl₂: 22.2 g; H₂O: 3.6 g; CO₂: 8.8 g. Calculate the missing mass and state the law you used.
items.answer: 20 g; conservation of mass (total mass of reactants 34.6 g = total mass of products).
items.markingKey: mass of reactants = mass of products (conservation of mass) [1]; missing mass = 20 g [1]

items.stem: Balance the equation: Al + HCl → AlCl₃ + H₂
items.answer: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂
items.markingKey: 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂ [2]

items.stem: Write the balanced symbol equation, with state symbols, for the reaction: potassium + water → potassium hydroxide + hydrogen.
items.answer: 2K(s) + 2H₂O(l) → 2KOH(aq) + H₂(g)
items.markingKey: 2K(s) + 2H₂O(l) → 2KOH(aq) + H₂(g): 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balancing; 1 mark state symbols [3]

items.stem: Tariq investigates the reaction: aluminium + hydrochloric acid → aluminium chloride + hydrogen. (a) Write the balanced symbol equation, including state symbols. (b) State the number of atoms of each element on the left-hand side. (c) Suggest why the mass of the reaction container may change if the reaction is done in an open beaker.
items.answer: (a) 2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2AlCl₃(aq) + 3H₂(g) (b) Al 2, Cl 6, H 6 (c) a gas is given off / taken in from the air
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balanced; 1 mark state symbols [3] (b) [1] (c) [1]

items.stem: Which ions are spectator ions in the reaction AgNO₃(aq) + KBr(aq) → AgBr(s) + KNO₃(aq)?
items.answer: K⁺ and NO₃⁻
items.markingKey: Ionic equation: Ag⁺(aq) + Br⁻(aq) → AgBr(s); the ions unchanged in solution are K⁺ and NO₃⁻.

items.stem: For the precipitation of lead(II) iodide from lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide, Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI(aq) → PbI₂(s) + 2KNO₃(aq), explain why K⁺ and NO₃⁻ are not included in the ionic equation, and write the ionic equation.
items.answer: K⁺ and NO₃⁻ are present in the same form, dissolved in solution, before and after the reaction (spectator ions). Ionic equation: Pb²⁺(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) → PbI₂(s).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: unchanged / remain in solution; 1 mark: ionic equation [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain how an ionic equation can be checked to make sure it is balanced. (b) A student writes the ionic equation for zinc reacting with copper(II) sulfate as Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Explain why this is not an ionic equation and give the correct one.
items.answer: (a) The numbers of each type of atom and the total charge must both be the same on each side. (b) It includes the sulfate spectator ion within formulae; the ionic equation is Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s).
items.markingKey: (a) [2] (b) 1 mark: spectator not removed; 1 mark: correct ionic equation [2]

items.stem: Nadia mixes aqueous magnesium nitrate with aqueous sodium carbonate. A precipitate of magnesium carbonate forms. Write the full balanced equation and the ionic equation, each with state symbols.
items.answer: Mg(NO₃)₂ + Na₂CO₃ → MgCO₃ + 2NaNO₃; Mg²⁺(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq) → MgCO₃(s)
items.markingKey: full: Mg(NO₃)₂ + Na₂CO₃ → MgCO₃ + 2NaNO₃ [1]; state symbols [1]; ionic: Mg²⁺(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq) → MgCO₃(s) [1]

items.stem: In a college laboratory, a student carries out the reaction of chlorine with sodium iodide solution: Cl₂ + 2NaI → 2NaCl + I₂. (a) Add state symbols to the full equation. (b) Identify the spectator ions. (c) Show that the ionic equation is balanced for charge. (d) Describe what would be observed during the reaction.
items.answer: (a) Cl₂(aq) + 2NaI(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + I₂(aq) (b) Na⁺ (c) total charge on the left equals total charge on the right (d) see observations: e.g. fizzing / colour change / temperature rise

items.stem: Which formula represents a molecule containing a total of five atoms?
items.answer: CH₄
items.markingKey: CH₄: 1 + 4 = 5 atoms.

items.stem: Carbon has a valency of 4 and hydrogen a valency of 1. Deduce the formula of the compound they form and explain your reasoning.
items.answer: CH₄
items.markingKey: Combining powers must match: CH₄ (methane) [2]

items.stem: Ana, a student in Dubai, is told that carbon has a valency of 4 and chlorine has a valency of 1. Deduce the formula of the covalent compound formed and explain how many bonds each atom makes.
items.answer: CCl₄ (tetrachloromethane): each carbon atom forms 4 bond(s) and each chlorine atom forms 1; the numbers of bonds must match.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: formula CCl₄; 1 mark: bonds per atom = valency; 1 mark: ratio so total bonds match [3]

items.stem: State the number of atoms of each element in the formula C₆H₁₂O₆, and the total number of atoms.
items.answer: C 6, H 12, O 6; total 24

items.stem: Use the charges on the ions to write the formula of each compound: sodium oxide, iron(II) fluoride.
items.answer: sodium oxide: Na₂O; iron(II) fluoride: FeF₂
items.markingKey: sodium oxide: Na₂O; iron(II) fluoride: FeF₂. 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: State the number of atoms of each element in the formula MgSO₄·7H₂O, and the total number of atoms.
items.answer: Mg 1, S 1, O 11, H 14; total 27

items.stem: Isla is labelling bottles of chemicals in a chemistry club. The bottles contain potassium hydroxide, ammonium chloride and ammonium carbonate. (a) Write the formula of each compound. (b) Explain why the formula of a compound containing a polyatomic ion sometimes needs brackets.
items.answer: (a) KOH; NH₄Cl; (NH₄)₂CO₃ (b) to show that the subscript multiplies the whole group of atoms in the ion
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each [3] (b) [1]

items.stem: A technician in Manila needs formulae for three compounds: ammonium bromide, ammonium sulfate and sodium sulfate. (a) Give the formula and charge of each ion present in the three compounds. (b) State the total number of atoms in the formula of ammonium bromide. (c) Explain why the formula of sodium sulfate contains the ions in that ratio.
items.answer: (a) NH₄⁺, Br⁻; NH₄⁺, SO₄²⁻; Na⁺, SO₄²⁻ (b) 6 (c) the total positive charge must equal the total negative charge (compound is neutral)
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per compound [3] (b) [1] (c) [2]

items.stem: In the equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, how many hydrogen atoms are shown on the left?
items.markingKey: 2 × H₂ = 4 H atoms.

items.stem: Kwame writes the equation for "carbon + oxygen → carbon monoxide" as C + O₂ → CO. Explain why the equation is not acceptable and write it correctly with state symbols.
items.answer: It is not balanced: the numbers of atoms of each element are not equal on both sides. Correct: 2C(s) + O₂(g) → 2CO(g).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: not balanced; 1 mark: correct balanced equation [2]

items.stem: Ravi writes the equation for "chlorine + potassium bromide → potassium chloride + bromine" as Cl₂ + KBr → KCl + Br₂. Explain why the equation is not acceptable and write it correctly with state symbols.
items.answer: It is not balanced: the numbers of atoms of each element are not equal on both sides. Correct: Cl₂(aq) + 2KBr(aq) → 2KCl(aq) + Br₂(aq).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: not balanced / atoms not conserved; 1 mark: correct coefficients; 1 mark: state symbols [3]

items.stem: Elena carries out the reaction 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O in a closed container. The masses of the substances that react and are formed are: C₄H₁₀: 232 g; O₂: 832 g; CO₂: 704 g; H₂O: ?. Calculate the missing mass and state the law you used.
items.answer: 360 g; conservation of mass (total mass of reactants 1064 g = total mass of products).
items.markingKey: mass of reactants = mass of products (conservation of mass) [1]; missing mass = 360 g [1]

items.stem: Balance the equation: Al + O₂ → Al₂O₃
items.answer: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃
items.markingKey: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ [2]

items.stem: Write the balanced symbol equation, with state symbols, for the reaction: propane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.
items.answer: C₃H₈(g) + 5O₂(g) → 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(l)
items.markingKey: C₃H₈(g) + 5O₂(g) → 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(l): 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balancing; 1 mark state symbols [3]

items.stem: Omar investigates the reaction: iron + chlorine → iron(III) chloride. (a) Write the balanced symbol equation, including state symbols. (b) State the number of atoms of each element on the left-hand side. (c) Calculate the relative formula mass of FeCl₃. (Ar: Cl = 35.5, Fe = 56)
items.answer: (a) 2Fe(s) + 3Cl₂(g) → 2FeCl₃(s) (b) Cl 6, Fe 2 (c) 162.5
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark formulae; 1 mark balanced; 1 mark state symbols [3] (b) [1] (c) 56 + 3 × 35.5 = 162.5 [1]

items.stem: Which ions are spectator ions in the reaction CuSO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Cu(OH)₂(s) + Na₂SO₄(aq)?
items.answer: Na⁺ and SO₄²⁻
items.markingKey: Ionic equation: Cu²⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq) → Cu(OH)₂(s); the ions unchanged in solution are Na⁺ and SO₄²⁻.

items.stem: For the reaction of iron with copper(II) sulfate solution, Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s), explain why SO₄²⁻ is not included in the ionic equation, and write the ionic equation.
items.answer: SO₄²⁻ is present in the same form, dissolved in solution, before and after the reaction (spectator ion). Ionic equation: Fe(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Fe²⁺(aq) + Cu(s).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: unchanged / remain in solution; 1 mark: ionic equation [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) A student writes the ionic equation for zinc reacting with copper(II) sulfate as Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Explain why this is not an ionic equation and give the correct one. (b) Explain why the ionic equation for the reaction of nitric acid with sodium hydroxide is the same as that for hydrochloric acid with potassium hydroxide.
items.answer: (a) It includes the sulfate spectator ion within formulae; the ionic equation is Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s). (b) In both, the only change is H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O; the metal ions and the acid anions are spectator ions that remain in solution unchanged.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: spectator not removed; 1 mark: correct ionic equation [2] (b) 1 mark: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O; 1 mark: other ions are spectators [2]

items.stem: The full equation for the precipitation of iron(III) hydroxide from iron(III) chloride and sodium hydroxide is FeCl₃(aq) + 3NaOH(aq) → Fe(OH)₃(s) + 3NaCl(aq). Write the ionic equation for this reaction, including state symbols, and identify the spectator ions.
items.answer: Fe³⁺(aq) + 3OH⁻(aq) → Fe(OH)₃(s); spectator ions: Na⁺ and Cl⁻
items.markingKey: Fe³⁺(aq) + 3OH⁻(aq) → Fe(OH)₃(s): 1 mark species; 1 mark balanced with states; 1 mark spectators Na⁺ and Cl⁻ [3]

items.stem: Samuel investigates the reaction of bromine with potassium iodide solution. The full equation is Br₂ + 2KI → 2KBr + I₂. (a) Identify the spectator ions. (b) Write the ionic equation with state symbols. (c) Show that the ionic equation is balanced for charge.
items.answer: (a) K⁺ (b) Br₂(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2Br⁻(aq) + I₂(aq) (c) total charge on the left equals total charge on the right
items.markingKey: (a) [1] (b) 1 mark species; 1 mark balanced with states [2] (c) [1]
